name: Independence and partition of British India
short_desc: British rule ends as India and Pakistan become independent, while partition brings mass displacement and communal violence.
date_note: Independence came on 14–15 August 1947; the boundary award followed on 17 August. Present-day Bangladesh locates eastern Bengal, then part of Pakistan. Violence and migration extended beyond these milestones.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. A major decolonization and population-displacement milestone absent despite existing Gandhi, Mughal and British-colonial subjects. Evidence and date rationale: Independence came on 14–15 August 1947, with the boundary award published on 17 August. Present-day Bangladesh locates eastern Bengal, then part of Pakistan; Bangladesh did not become independent in 1947. Violence and migration extended beyond these formal milestones. Primary evidence: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/teaching-resources/partition-of-british-india/. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
